name: ebitda_l2_growth_roic_size
mechanism: Under a constant-growth DCF, EV/EBITDA rises with expected growth and with the return on new investment (high ROIC means less reinvestment per unit of growth), and larger firms trade at lower risk premia. Restricting to the 2-digit industry keeps shared business risk while ranking on growth, ROIC and size picks peers with the same fundamental value drivers inside a deeper pool than L3.
prediction: Median |ln(V_est/V)| below the L3 industry-median baseline (0.333) in at least 3 of 4 exploration years.
compact: EV/EBITDA | screen same industry_l2 | rank sales_growth_1y 1.5, roic 1, log_sales 1 | k=10, median, min_peers=5 | fallback []
critic_reason: Constant-growth DCF logic (EV/EBITDA rises with growth, with ROIC through lower reinvestment, and falls with risk proxied by size) is specific and sensible, the L2 screen plus growth/ROIC/size ranking implements it directly, nothing similar has been tried, and the year-by-year comparison against a stated baseline is falsifiable.

name: ebitda_l3_capex_growth
mechanism: EBITDA ignores the depreciation and capital spending needed to sustain it, so capital-heavy firms convert less EBITDA into free cash flow and deserve lower EV/EBITDA. Within the 3-digit industry, matching on capex intensity and growth aligns the EBITDA-to-FCF conversion and growth outlook that drive the multiple.
prediction: Overall exploration median error at or below 0.325 and beats the L3 industry median in at least 3 of 4 years.
compact: EV/EBITDA | screen same industry_l3 | rank capex_intensity 1.5, sales_growth_1y 1, ebitda_margin 0.5 | k=8, median, min_peers=5 | fallback [same industry_l2] -> []
critic_reason: Capex intensity driving how much EBITDA turns into free cash flow is a specific, well-grounded driver of EV/EBITDA, the L3 screen with capex-intensity-led ranking matches it, it is a new economic idea, and the error threshold plus 3-of-4-years test is falsifiable.

name: ebitda_l4_size_harmonic
mechanism: The narrowest industry definition captures the most similar products, customers and cyclicality, and the harmonic mean is the theoretically consistent average of price ratios (it averages the yield EBITDA/EV) and damps high-multiple outliers. Ranking on size and asset turnover within the narrow industry further aligns scale-driven risk and business model.
prediction: Lower median error than the L3 industry median in at least 3 of 4 years, with a lower mean error than 0.513.
compact: EV/EBITDA | screen same industry_l4 | rank log_assets 1, asset_turnover 1 | k=6, harmonic_mean, min_peers=4 | fallback [same industry_l3] -> [same industry_l2]
critic_reason: Narrow-industry matching (shared products, customers, cyclicality) and the harmonic mean as the consistent average of price ratios are both sensible and implemented through the L4 screen, fallbacks and aggregator, and the prediction is falsifiable; note that the asset-turnover ranking is only loosely justified ('business model'), and the recipe bundles three changes together, so a win or loss will not show which part caused it.

name: sales_l2_margin_matched
mechanism: EV/Sales equals EV/EBITDA times the EBITDA margin, so most cross-sectional dispersion in EV/Sales comes from profitability differences. Within a 2-digit industry, ranking peers primarily on EBITDA margin and secondarily on gross margin and growth removes the dominant source of error that plain industry medians ignore.
prediction: Median error below 0.50, beating the EV/Sales L3 industry median (0.603) in all 4 exploration years.
compact: EV/Sales | screen same industry_l2 | rank ebitda_margin 3, gross_margin 1, sales_growth_1y 1 | k=8, median, min_peers=5 | fallback []
critic_reason: The identity EV/Sales = EV/EBITDA x EBITDA margin gives a specific reason why margin-matched peers should share EV/Sales, the heavy EBITDA-margin weight inside L2 implements it exactly, and beating the L3 median in all 4 years with median error below 0.50 is clearly falsifiable.

name: sales_crossindustry_margin_band
mechanism: If EV/Sales is mostly profitability times a growth- and risk-driven EBITDA multiple, then firms with near-identical EBITDA margins, growth and size should share EV/Sales even across industries. A hard band on EBITDA margin forces profitability equality, and ranking on growth, ROIC and size handles the remaining multiple drivers.
prediction: Beats the EV/Sales L3 industry median in at least 3 of 4 years; median error below 0.55.
compact: EV/Sales | screen band ebitda_margin±0.04 | rank ebitda_margin 2, sales_growth_1y 1, roic 1, log_sales 0.5 | k=12, median, min_peers=5 | fallback [band ebitda_margin±0.1] -> []
critic_reason: Testing whether matching on fundamentals (margin band plus growth/ROIC/size) can replace industry membership for EV/Sales is a distinct, economically motivated hypothesis that the margin band and ranking implement faithfully, and it is falsifiable; the proposer should expect it to fail if industry-level risk or cyclicality that these features do not capture matters.

name: sales_l3_margin_growth_harmonic
mechanism: Within the 3-digit industry, firms with the same EBITDA margin and growth have the same cash-flow-per-dollar-of-sales and similar duration, so their EV/Sales should coincide; the harmonic mean limits the upward pull of a few richly priced peers that commonly inflate EV/Sales averages.
prediction: Median error below 0.52 overall and lower than the EV/Sales industry median in every exploration year.
compact: EV/Sales | screen same industry_l3 | rank ebitda_margin 2.5, sales_growth_1y 1, log_sales 0.5 | k=6, harmonic_mean, min_peers=4 | fallback [same industry_l2] -> []
critic_reason: Matching on EBITDA margin and growth within L3 to align cash flow per dollar of sales and duration is sensible and implemented by the ranking, and the L3-with-L2-fallback screen, log_sales feature and harmonic mean make it more than a trivial variant of proposal 3 (it tests pool depth and aggregation); the every-year claim is falsifiable.

name: evs_l2_margin_band_hybrid
mechanism: EV/Sales is the EBITDA margin times an EBITDA multiple. The margin band equalizes the margin, and the shared 2-digit industry equalizes the multiple's industry-level risk, cyclicality and growth. Requiring both conditions together should remove the profitability error that plain industry medians make, and also the business-risk mismatch that a pure cross-industry margin match allows. When the industry-plus-band pool is too thin, the rule falls back to the cross-industry margin band, so coverage stays complete.
prediction: Beats the industry median in 4 of 4 years and reaches an exploration median error below 0.43 (at or better than the pure cross-industry margin-band recipe).
compact: EV/Sales | screen same industry_l2, band ebitda_margin±0.05 | rank ebitda_margin 2, sales_growth_1y 1, log_sales 0.5 | k=8, median, min_peers=4 | fallback [band ebitda_margin±0.05] -> [band ebitda_margin±0.1]
critic_reason: Combining the 2-digit industry screen with an EBITDA-margin band is a new screen that directly follows the stated decomposition EV/Sales = margin x EBITDA multiple. The industry screen holds the multiple's risk and cyclicality fixed and the band holds the margin fixed, the cross-industry fallback keeps coverage, and the prediction is falsifiable.

name: evs_margin_growth_double_band
mechanism: With the margin held fixed, what is left of the EV/Sales multiple depends mainly on expected growth and on how much reinvestment that growth needs. Hard bands on both EBITDA margin and 1-year growth fix the two largest drivers. Ranking on capital intensity and ROIC then lines up the free-cash-flow conversion of each sales dollar.
prediction: Beats the industry median in at least 3 of 4 years, with a mean absolute log error below 0.65.
compact: EV/Sales | screen band ebitda_margin±0.04, band sales_growth_1y±0.15 | rank ebitda_margin 2, capex_intensity 1, roic 1, log_assets 0.5 | k=10, median, min_peers=5 | fallback [band ebitda_margin±0.04] -> [band ebitda_margin±0.1]
critic_reason: Adding a hard 1-year growth band to the margin band, and ranking on capex intensity and ROIC (which set reinvestment and FCF conversion), is a new screen that implements the stated margin-growth-reinvestment logic. Be aware that 1-year growth is a noisy stand-in for expected growth.

name: evs_cost_structure_band
mechanism: Two firms can have the same EBITDA margin while earning it through different cost structures. A high-gross-margin, high-opex firm, such as software, has more pricing power and operating leverage than a low-gross-margin, lean-opex firm, such as distribution. Banding on both gross margin and EBITDA margin matches pricing power and cost structure across industries. Ranking on growth, capital intensity and size then handles duration and risk, and a trimmed mean limits the effect of extreme peers.
prediction: Beats the industry median in 4 of 4 years, with an exploration median error below 0.50.
compact: EV/Sales | screen band gross_margin±0.08, band ebitda_margin±0.05 | rank sales_growth_1y 1.5, capex_intensity 1, log_sales 0.5 | k=10, trimmed_mean, min_peers=5 | fallback [band ebitda_margin±0.05] -> [band ebitda_margin±0.1]
critic_reason: A gross-margin band is a new screen with a clear cost-structure and pricing-power reason for matching multiples at a given EBITDA margin, and the recipe implements it. Note that higher operating leverage also means higher risk, which pulls the multiple the other way, so the expected sign is not certain.

name: eve_l2_da_burden_match
mechanism: EBITDA leaves out depreciation and amortization, so it overstates the cash earnings of firms with heavy asset bases. The gap between EBITDA margin and EBIT margin measures this D&A burden, and capex intensity measures the reinvestment needed going forward. Within the 2-digit industry, matching both margins together with capex and growth picks peers that turn EBITDA into free cash flow at the same rate.
prediction: Beats the industry median in at least 3 of 4 years, with an exploration median error below 0.330.
compact: EV/EBITDA | screen same industry_l2 | rank capex_intensity 1.5, ebit_margin 1, ebitda_margin 1, sales_growth_1y 1, log_sales 0.5 | k=10, median, min_peers=5 | fallback []
critic_reason: Matching EBITDA and EBIT margins together pins down the D&A share of EBITDA, a known driver of EV/EBITDA differences. This is a new feature and a new economic idea, not a trivial variant of g01-01 or g01-02, and the prediction is falsifiable.

name: eve_l2_growth_band
mechanism: In a constant-growth valuation, EV/EBITDA depends most on expected growth, just as EV/Sales depends most on margin. A hard band on 1-year sales growth within the 2-digit industry forces peers to have similar growth. Ranking on capex intensity and ROIC then lines up how much reinvestment that growth costs.
prediction: Beats the industry median in at least 3 of 4 years, with a mean absolute log error below 0.50.
compact: EV/EBITDA | screen same industry_l2, band sales_growth_1y±0.1 | rank capex_intensity 1, roic 1, log_sales 0.5 | k=8, median, min_peers=5 | fallback [same industry_l2] -> []
critic_reason: A hard 1-year growth band inside the 2-digit industry is a new screen for EV/EBITDA that follows the stated constant-growth logic, with capex and ROIC ranking for the cost of reinvestment. Expect thin pools: realized 1-year growth only loosely tracks expected growth.

name: eve_cross_industry_fundamentals
mechanism: If EV/EBITDA is set by growth, reinvestment needs and risk rather than by industry labels, then firms with similar growth and EBITDA margins should share a multiple across industries. The margin band also stands in for competitive position. Ranking on capex intensity, ROIC and size then matches free-cash-flow conversion and the risk premium. This recipe tests whether the cross-industry fundamental matching that works for EV/Sales also works for EV/EBITDA.
prediction: Reaches an exploration median error at or below the industry median's 0.333 and beats it in at least 2 of 4 years.
compact: EV/EBITDA | screen band ebitda_margin±0.05, band sales_growth_1y±0.1 | rank capex_intensity 1.5, roic 1, log_sales 1 | k=15, median, min_peers=5 | fallback [band sales_growth_1y±0.1] -> []
critic_reason: This is a clean, falsifiable test of whether growth, reinvestment (capex and ROIC) and size can replace industry labels for EV/EBITDA. Be aware that EBITDA margin is not a theoretical driver of EV/EBITDA, so the margin band mostly adds noise, and dropping the industry screen may lose risk information the accounting features do not capture.

name: g03-01 industry-plus-cost-structure EV/Sales
mechanism: EV/Sales equals EBITDA margin times an EBITDA multiple. The multiple itself depends on industry risk and on pricing power, which shows up in gross margin. Requiring the same 2-digit industry together with matching gross and EBITDA margins equalizes profitability, cost structure and business risk all at once. Ranking on growth, capex intensity and size then lines up duration and reinvestment needs. Fallbacks to the cross-industry double band and then a wide EBITDA band keep coverage high.
prediction: Median |ln error| below 0.391, the best archived EV/Sales recipe, and beats the industry median in all 4 exploration years.
compact: EV/Sales | screen same industry_l2, band gross_margin±0.1, band ebitda_margin±0.05 | rank sales_growth_1y 1.5, capex_intensity 1, log_sales 0.5 | k=8, median, min_peers=4 | fallback [band gross_margin±0.08, band ebitda_margin±0.05] -> [band ebitda_margin±0.1]
critic_reason: Adding a same-2-digit-industry screen on top of the gross- and EBITDA-margin double band (g02-03) is a new screen with a clear rationale (industry risk plus pricing power plus profitability), the recipe implements it, and the 0.391 target is falsifiable.

name: g03-02 nested industry hierarchy with margin band EV/Sales
mechanism: The narrowest industry that still has enough margin-matched peers gives the closest business risk and growth outlook. Starting from the 3-digit industry inside an EBITDA-margin band and widening step by step (2-digit plus band, then band alone, then a wider band) uses the most specific valid peer group for each firm. Ranking on EBITDA margin, gross margin and growth handles any profitability gap left inside the band.
prediction: Beats the industry median in 4 of 4 years, with median |ln error| at or below 0.40.

spec.name: g03-02 nested industry hierarchy with margin band EV/Sales

compact: EV/Sales | screen same industry_l3, band ebitda_margin±0.05 | rank ebitda_margin 2, gross_margin 1, sales_growth_1y 1, log_sales 0.5 | k=6, median, min_peers=4 | fallback [same industry_l2, band ebitda_margin±0.05] -> [band ebitda_margin±0.05] -> [band ebitda_margin±0.1]
critic_reason: Starting from a 3-digit-industry-plus-margin-band peer set and widening step by step is a new screen structure, not just a k/weight tweak of g02-01, and it matches the most-specific-valid-peer-group mechanism; note that the 0.40 target would not beat the archived 0.391, so a pass would not show progress.

name: g03-03 free-cash-flow margin match EV/Sales
mechanism: What sales are worth depends on the free cash flow each dollar of sales produces, which is roughly EBITDA margin minus capex intensity. Two firms with the same EBITDA margin but very different capex needs convert sales to cash at very different rates. Hard bands on both EBITDA margin and capex intensity match FCF margin across industries. Ranking on growth, gross margin (pricing power) and size then handles duration and risk.
prediction: Median |ln error| below 0.429 (the plain cross-industry EBITDA-margin band) and beats the industry median in all 4 years.
compact: EV/Sales | screen band ebitda_margin±0.05, band capex_intensity±0.03 | rank sales_growth_1y 1.5, gross_margin 1, log_sales 0.5 | k=10, median, min_peers=5 | fallback [band ebitda_margin±0.05] -> [band ebitda_margin±0.1]
critic_reason: A hard capex-intensity band alongside the EBITDA-margin band is a new screen that directly carries out the FCF-margin (EBITDA margin minus capex) mechanism across industries, and the 0.429 target is falsifiable.

name: g03-04 pricing-power and reinvestment EV/EBITDA
mechanism: Inside an industry, firms with high gross margins tend to have durable moats and pricing power. Their EBITDA is more persistent and earns a higher multiple. Capex intensity and EBIT margin measure how much of EBITDA is used up by reinvestment and depreciation. Ranking 2-digit industry peers on gross margin, capex, EBIT margin and growth matches both how durable the earnings are and how much of them turns into cash.
prediction: Median |ln error| at or below 0.320 and beats the industry median in at least 3 of 4 years.
compact: EV/EBITDA | screen same industry_l2 | rank gross_margin 1, capex_intensity 1.5, ebit_margin 1, sales_growth_1y 1, log_assets 0.5 | k=12, median, min_peers=5
critic_reason: Swapping EBITDA margin for gross margin as a pricing-power/durability ranking feature is a new feature and a new economic idea for EV/EBITDA relative to g02-04, and the ranking matches the mechanism; it is close to g02-04, though, so read the result as a test of gross margin specifically.

name: g03-05 distress-adjusted EV/EBITDA
mechanism: EV is unlevered in theory, but heavily indebted firms carry expected distress costs and less financial flexibility, which pushes down their EV/EBITDA. Within the 2-digit industry, matching on net debt to EBITDA together with capex intensity, EBIT margin and growth aligns the distress discount, cash conversion and growth outlook. A trimmed mean limits the influence of distressed or richly priced outliers.
prediction: Beats the industry median in at least 3 of 4 years, with a mean |ln error| below 0.49.
compact: EV/EBITDA | screen same industry_l2 | rank capex_intensity 1.5, ebit_margin 1, sales_growth_1y 1, net_debt_to_ebitda 1, log_sales 0.5 | k=10, trimmed_mean, min_peers=5
critic_reason: Net debt to EBITDA is a new feature with a specific distress-discount mechanism, and ranking on it within the 2-digit industry implements that mechanism; however, switching to a trimmed mean at the same time confounds what any change can be credited to.

name: g03-06 hard capex screen EV/EBITDA
mechanism: Capex intensity has been the strongest ranking signal for EV/EBITDA, because it sets how much EBITDA must be reinvested to sustain the business. Turning it into a hard band within the 2-digit industry means no peer has a very different reinvestment burden. Ranking on EBIT and EBITDA margins (the D&A gap) plus growth and size then sorts out the remaining differences in value drivers.
prediction: Median |ln error| below 0.333 (industry median) in at least 3 of 4 years and overall median at or below 0.320.
compact: EV/EBITDA | screen same industry_l2, band capex_intensity±0.04 | rank ebit_margin 1, ebitda_margin 1, sales_growth_1y 1, log_sales 0.5 | k=8, median, min_peers=5 | fallback [same industry_l2] -> []
critic_reason: Turning capex intensity from a ranking weight into a hard within-industry band is a new screen that enforces matching reinvestment burdens as the mechanism claims, and both error targets are falsifiable.

name: g04-01 R&D-inclusive reinvestment peers (EV/EBITDA)
mechanism: R&D is expensed, so it lowers reported EBITDA even though it is an investment in future earnings, much like capex. R&D-heavy firms therefore show depressed EBITDA relative to their economic earnings and trade at higher EV/EBITDA. Within the 2-digit industry, matching on R&D intensity together with capex intensity, gross margin, EBIT margin and growth aligns total reinvestment (tangible plus intangible), pricing power and growth.
prediction: Median error below 0.315 and beats the industry median in all 4 exploration years, with the largest gains in R&D-heavy industries (SIC 28, 35, 36, 38, 73); coverage of at least 90%.
compact: EV/EBITDA | screen same industry_l2 | rank capex_intensity 1.5, rnd_intensity 1, gross_margin 1, ebit_margin 1, sales_growth_1y 1, log_assets 0.5 | k=12, median, min_peers=5 | fallback []
critic_reason: Adds a genuinely new feature (rnd_intensity) with a sound reason, since expensed R&D depresses EBITDA the way unexpensed capex does not, and the recipe ranks on it directly. The 90% coverage claim is falsifiable and worth checking, because candidates missing R&D are dropped.

name: g04-02 Moat, reinvestment, distress and ROIC with harmonic mean (EV/EBITDA)
mechanism: EV/EBITDA rises with earnings durability (gross margin), falls with the reinvestment burden (capex intensity) and with distress costs (net debt to EBITDA), and rises with ROIC because high-return firms need less reinvestment per unit of growth. Matching all four drivers plus growth inside the 2-digit industry gives a wider peer set (k=15). Aggregating with the harmonic mean averages the earnings yields EBITDA/EV, which are roughly linear in these drivers, so a few richly priced peers do not pull the estimate up.
prediction: Beats the industry median in at least 3 of 4 years, with a mean error below 0.480 (lower than the median-aggregated archive recipes) because the harmonic mean controls overvaluation errors.

spec.name: g04-02 Moat, reinvestment, distress and ROIC with harmonic mean (EV/EBITDA)

compact: EV/EBITDA | screen same industry_l2 | rank gross_margin 1, capex_intensity 1.5, net_debt_to_ebitda 1, roic 0.75, sales_growth_1y 1, log_assets 0.5 | k=15, harmonic_mean, min_peers=5 | fallback []
critic_reason: Every rank feature (gross margin, capex intensity, net debt/EBITDA, ROIC, growth, size) has already been tried in g03-04, g03-05 and g02-05, so the part that is actually new is the harmonic-mean aggregator and a larger k, which the rules count as a trivial variant.
reason: critic: Every rank feature (gross margin, capex intensity, net debt/EBITDA, ROIC, growth, size) has already been tried in g03-04, g03-05 and g02-05, so the part that is actually new is the harmonic-mean aggregator and a larger k, which the rules count as a trivial variant.

name: g04-03 Transitory-earnings matching (EV/EBITDA)
mechanism: When EBITDA is temporarily depressed, EV/EBITDA is temporarily high, because the market values normalized earnings rather than the current year's. Firms whose net margin is far below their EBITDA margin, with weak 1-year growth and low ROE, are more likely to be at a cyclical trough or carrying heavy D&A, interest or one-off charges. Within the 2-digit industry, matching on EBITDA margin, net margin, ROE, growth and capex intensity picks peers in the same phase of earnings, and a trimmed mean removes trough-multiple outliers.
prediction: Beats the industry median in at least 3 of 4 years, and median error below 0.325.
compact: EV/EBITDA | screen same industry_l2 | rank capex_intensity 1.5, ebitda_margin 1, net_margin 1, roe 0.5, sales_growth_1y 1, log_assets 0.5 | k=12, trimmed_mean, min_peers=5 | fallback []
critic_reason: The recipe does not implement the mechanism: 'temporarily depressed' EBITDA is relative to a firm's own normal earnings, but ranking on current-year levels of EBITDA margin, net margin and ROE cannot tell a firm at a cyclical trough from one whose margins are structurally low or whose gap comes from permanent D&A or leverage. Isolating transitory earnings needs a time-series signal such as a margin change against history.
reason: critic: The recipe does not implement the mechanism: 'temporarily depressed' EBITDA is relative to a firm's own normal earnings, but ranking on current-year levels of EBITDA margin, net margin and ROE cannot tell a firm at a cyclical trough from one whose margins are structurally low or whose gap comes from permanent D&A or leverage. Isolating transitory earnings needs a time-series signal such as a margin change against history.

name: g04-04 EBIT-margin band within industry (EV/Sales)
mechanism: Sales are worth what they convert into sustainable cash flow. EBIT margin, which subtracts D&A as a proxy for maintenance capex, is closer to that than EBITDA margin, because it does not overstate the cash margin of asset-heavy firms. A hard EBIT-margin band inside the 2-digit industry matches after-reinvestment profitability and business risk together. Ranking on EBIT and EBITDA margin (which also captures the D&A gap), growth, gross margin and size then sorts out the remaining differences.
prediction: Median error below 0.380 and beats the industry median in all 4 years.
compact: EV/Sales | screen same industry_l2, band ebit_margin±0.04 | rank ebit_margin 2, ebitda_margin 1, sales_growth_1y 1, gross_margin 0.5, log_sales 0.5 | k=8, median, min_peers=4 | fallback [band ebit_margin±0.04] -> [band ebit_margin±0.08] -> [band ebitda_margin±0.1]
critic_reason: A hard EBIT-margin band is a new screen with a clear rationale: for EV/Sales, an after-D&A margin is a better proxy for sustainable cash conversion than EBITDA margin, especially for asset-heavy firms. The band and the rank features match that idea.

name: g04-05 Value-creating growth: ROIC x growth (EV/Sales)
mechanism: Once the margin is fixed, the EBITDA multiple embedded in EV/Sales depends on growth, but growth only adds value when ROIC exceeds the cost of capital. Growth at low ROIC can even destroy value. Inside the 2-digit industry plus an EBITDA-margin band, ranking with equal heavy weights on ROIC and 1-year growth picks peers whose growth creates value at the same rate.
prediction: Beats the industry median in all 4 years, and median error below 0.385.

spec.name: g04-05 Value-creating growth: ROIC x growth (EV/Sales)

compact: EV/Sales | screen same industry_l2, band ebitda_margin±0.05 | rank roic 1.5, sales_growth_1y 1.5, ebitda_margin 1, log_sales 0.5 | k=8, median, min_peers=4 | fallback [band ebitda_margin±0.05] -> [band ebitda_margin±0.1]
critic_reason: Sound value-driver logic: once the margin is fixed, growth adds to the multiple only to the extent ROIC exceeds the cost of capital. Weighting ROIC and growth heavily inside an industry plus margin band implements this, and it differs from g02-01 (adds ROIC) and from g01-05 (adds the industry screen and puts ROIC on equal footing with growth).

name: g04-06 Hierarchical cost-structure match (EV/Sales)
mechanism: The best peers share both the narrowest industry (product market, cyclicality) and the same cost structure (gross margin and EBITDA margin). The rule first requires the 3-digit industry with both margin bands. If that is too thin, it widens to the 2-digit industry with both bands, then to the cross-industry double band, then to a wide EBITDA band. This way each firm gets the most specific peer group that matches both pricing power and profitability. Ranking on growth, capex intensity, EBITDA margin and size handles the remaining duration and reinvestment differences.
prediction: Median error below 0.370, beats the industry median in all 4 years, and coverage of at least 93%.
compact: EV/Sales | screen same industry_l3, band gross_margin±0.1, band ebitda_margin±0.05 | rank sales_growth_1y 1.5, capex_intensity 1, ebitda_margin 1, log_sales 0.5 | k=6, median, min_peers=4 | fallback [same industry_l2, band gross_margin±0.1, band ebitda_margin±0.05] -> [band gross_margin±0.08, band ebitda_margin±0.05] -> [band ebitda_margin±0.1]
critic_reason: This is essentially g03-01 with a 3-digit tier added in front of the same fallback chain (already explored in g03-02), k cut from 8 to 6, and an EBITDA-margin rank feature that adds little inside a ±0.05 EBITDA band. That counts as a trivial recombination of recipes already tried, not a new screen or idea.
reason: critic: This is essentially g03-01 with a 3-digit tier added in front of the same fallback chain (already explored in g03-02), k cut from 8 to 6, and an EBITDA-margin rank feature that adds little inside a ±0.05 EBITDA band. That counts as a trivial recombination of recipes already tried, not a new screen or idea.

name: g05-01 size-banded discount rate peers (EV/EBITDA)
mechanism: Small firms carry higher discount rates (size, illiquidity and survival risk), so at the same cash conversion and growth they trade at systematically lower EV/EBITDA. Soft size weights in earlier recipes let a tiny firm be priced off giants whenever margins and capex matched. A hard log-sales band within the 2-digit industry makes size-driven risk a precondition, and ranking on capex intensity, EBIT margin, gross margin and growth then matches cash conversion and durability among similarly sized peers.
prediction: Beats the industry median in all 4 years and achieves median error at or below 0.315; the gain should be largest for the smallest size quintile of targets.
compact: EV/EBITDA | screen same industry_l2, band log_sales±1 | rank capex_intensity 1.5, ebit_margin 1, gross_margin 1, sales_growth_1y 1 | k=10, median, min_peers=5 | fallback [same industry_l2] -> []
critic_reason: A hard log-sales band inside the 2-digit industry is a new screen that directly implements a sensible size/discount-rate mechanism (earlier recipes only used soft size weights), and the prediction that gains concentrate in the smallest size quintile makes it clearly falsifiable.

name: g05-02 capital base and return on capital (EV/EBITDA)
mechanism: Capex intensity measures only the current flow of reinvestment, while asset turnover captures the whole capital base a business needs per dollar of sales, including working capital and acquired intangibles. EV/EBITDA rises when growth can be financed with little capital at a high ROIC. Ranking 2-digit industry peers on asset turnover, ROIC, capex intensity and growth matches the stock and flow of required capital and the return earned on it.
prediction: Beats the industry median in at least 3 of 4 years with median error below 0.325.

spec.name: g05-02 capital base and return on capital (EV/EBITDA)

compact: EV/EBITDA | screen same industry_l2 | rank asset_turnover 1.5, roic 1, capex_intensity 1.5, sales_growth_1y 1, log_assets 0.5 | k=12, median, min_peers=5 | fallback []
critic_reason: Adding asset turnover (the full capital base per dollar of sales) alongside ROIC and growth for EV/EBITDA implements the value-driver logic that growth funded at high ROIC with little capital earns a higher multiple, and it is a substantive change from g04-02 rather than a reweighting; a sharper subgroup prediction would strengthen it.

name: g05-03 earnings waterfall shape (EV/EBITDA)
mechanism: How EBITDA flows down to net income (through D&A, interest, taxes and recurring special charges) shows how much of it reaches capital providers as sustainable earnings. Two firms with the same EBITDA margin but very different net margins differ in D&A burden, leverage or recurring write-offs, all of which lower the multiple investors pay per dollar of EBITDA. Matching the whole margin waterfall (EBITDA, EBIT and net margin) plus capex intensity and growth within the 2-digit industry picks peers whose EBITDA is of similar quality.
prediction: Beats the industry median in all 4 years; median error below 0.320 and mean error below 0.485.
compact: EV/EBITDA | screen same industry_l2 | rank ebitda_margin 1, ebit_margin 1, net_margin 1, capex_intensity 1.5, sales_growth_1y 1 | k=10, median, min_peers=5 | fallback []
critic_reason: This is essentially the union of g02-04 (capex, EBIT and EBITDA margin, growth) and g04-03 (capex, EBITDA and net margin, growth) with size dropped, so it adds no new feature, screen or idea; also, net margin mixes in leverage and interest, which should not drive an enterprise-level EV/EBITDA multiple except through distress, so the 'EBITDA quality' story is only loosely matched by the features.

name: g05-04 R&D-adjusted economic margin (EV/Sales)
mechanism: R&D is expensed, so among firms with the same reported EBITDA margin, the R&D-heavy ones have higher economic margins and longer-lived growth options, and their sales are worth more. Inside the 2-digit industry plus an EBITDA-margin band, ranking on R&D intensity matches the share of the margin that is hidden investment. Gross margin and growth then line up pricing power and duration.
prediction: Beats the industry median in all 4 years with median error at or below 0.385; gains concentrated in R&D-intensive industries (SIC 28, 35, 36, 38, 73).
compact: EV/Sales | screen same industry_l2, band ebitda_margin±0.05 | rank rnd_intensity 1.5, gross_margin 1, sales_growth_1y 1, log_sales 0.5 | k=8, median, min_peers=4 | fallback [band ebitda_margin±0.05] -> [band ebitda_margin±0.1]
critic_reason: Ranking on R&D intensity within a reported-EBITDA-margin band is a new feature for EV/Sales and directly targets the expensed-investment wedge between reported and economic margin, with a falsifiable industry-concentrated prediction; watch coverage, because candidates with missing R&D are dropped, which can thin peer sets in non-R&D industries.

name: g05-05 leverage distress discount at fixed margin (EV/Sales)
mechanism: With profitability fixed by an EBITDA-margin band, highly levered firms suffer expected distress costs, underinvestment and lost flexibility that lower enterprise value per dollar of sales. Firms with net cash are often priced as having optionality. Ranking margin-matched 2-digit industry peers on net debt to EBITDA, together with growth and capex intensity, aligns the distress discount and the reinvestment burden that the margin alone does not capture.
prediction: Beats the industry median in all 4 years with median error below 0.390; improvement over g02-01 shows up mainly among targets with net debt/EBITDA above 3.

spec.name: g05-05 leverage distress discount at fixed margin (EV/Sales)

compact: EV/Sales | screen same industry_l2, band ebitda_margin±0.05 | rank net_debt_to_ebitda 1.5, sales_growth_1y 1.5, capex_intensity 1, log_sales 0.5 | k=8, median, min_peers=4 | fallback [band ebitda_margin±0.05] -> [band ebitda_margin±0.1]
critic_reason: Using net debt/EBITDA to capture the distress discount at a fixed margin is a new economic idea for the EV/Sales recipes, the recipe implements it directly, and the prediction that gains concentrate among targets with net debt/EBITDA above 3 is falsifiable; note that the ratio behaves badly when EBITDA is near zero or negative, which the margin band only partly contains.

name: g05-06 capital-turnover decomposition (EV/Sales)
mechanism: EV/Sales equals EV/invested capital divided by sales/invested capital. The first term is set by ROIC relative to the cost of capital, and the second by capital turnover. A hard asset-turnover band within the 2-digit industry fixes the capital needed per dollar of sales. Ranking on ROIC, then EBITDA margin and growth, fixes the value created per dollar of capital, so the recipe matches both factors of the decomposition rather than margin alone.
prediction: Beats the industry median in all 4 years; median error below 0.40, testing whether turnover-plus-ROIC matching can rival the EBITDA-margin band approach.
compact: EV/Sales | screen same industry_l2, band asset_turnover±0.3 | rank roic 2, ebitda_margin 1.5, sales_growth_1y 1, log_sales 0.5 | k=8, median, min_peers=4 | fallback [band asset_turnover±0.3, band ebitda_margin±0.05] -> [band ebitda_margin±0.05] -> [band ebitda_margin±0.1]
critic_reason: The EV/Sales = (EV/IC) x (IC/Sales) decomposition is a correct, specific mechanism: a hard asset-turnover band fixes the capital per dollar of sales and ROIC ranking fixes value per dollar of capital, which is new relative to the margin-band recipes; be aware that a fixed +/-0.3 turnover width is loose for low-turnover firms and tight for high-turnover ones, and that the last two fallbacks drop the turnover screen entirely.
